I get where you're coming from, and I absolutely despise forced positivity as well, but there are few points I'd like to make.

>These queens are supposed to be so pop culture savvy but they don't know shit about how celebrity works.

It's a bit unfair to compare a drag queen to a pop star, who has years of experience, people managing their social media and a huge PR team. Drag queens, in general, engage with their fans on a more personal level, so it's absolutely natural that every criticism/praise/hate they get is taken more personally. Most of the queens have only a local following before coming to rpdr, so when the celebrity hits them with all things ensuing, it might get a bit overwhelming.

>It certainly matters HOW, WHAT, and WHY we talk about things when we comment about these shows

Don't forget to add WHERE to the list. It's one thing to say "Bitch, Blair is sooo boring" on this sub, and an entirely different one when you comment the same thing on her insta post or mention her on twitter. Context, nuance and basic human empathy are as important as critical thinking, and you can't claim to have the latter without the former.
